The OpenSearch 'errors' profile query failed (SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR), so error evidence from that source is absent; the zero-error figures come from the JMeter sample summaries and the policy check in their own scopes.

Counting scopes differ: the metric summaries cover the whole run (37,349 samples) while the policy check denominator (36,034) covers only the run-intersection window; these are different quantities measuring different scopes and windows, not an inconsistency.
Clock alignment is 'not_verified_by_core', so no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal claims are supported; verify clocks before any time-based correlation.

No capacity bound or saturation point is established by this evidence; resource readings alone do not support headroom claims, and no resource policy defines materiality.

Resource statistics are interval means at a 15-second step (aggregation 'interval_mean', step_ms 15000), so sub-interval peaks are averaged out and not visible in the reported maxima; CPU is in cores and memory in bytes.

The business PASS applies to the run-intersection evaluation window (1790619855000 to 1790620200000), which excludes the trimmed leading (10,309 ms) and trailing (4,660 ms) portions of the run; whole-run metrics and window counts are different quantities.
